author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: گر زبان خواهی که باشد ترجمان / دل بباید پاک چون آب روان
english_translation: If you want your tongue to be a true interpreter / Your heart must be pure, like flowing water.
theme: Authentic speech flows only from a pure and sincere heart

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: آفتاب آمد دلیل آفتاب / گر دلیلت باید از وی رو متاب
english_translation: The sun itself is the proof of the sun / If you need proof of it, do not turn away from it.
theme: Divine truth is self-evident to those who do not turn away from it

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: آتش عشق است کاندر نی فتاد / مرد عاشق شد جدا از اهل راد
english_translation: The fire of love has fallen into the reed / The true lover has become separate from those of ordinary standing.
theme: Love as a transformative fire that separates the devoted from the ordinary

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: صبر کن با درد، درمانت کند / صبر کن با غم، خوشانت کند
english_translation: Be patient with pain, it will heal you / Be patient with sorrow, it will make you joyful.
theme: Enduring pain and sorrow with patience as the path to healing and joy

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: هر که را درد است، او برده است گوی / بی‌درد، نی جستجو دارد نه روی
english_translation: Whoever has pain has won the prize / Without pain, there is neither search nor face.
theme: Pain as the essential catalyst for spiritual seeking and growth

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: نی حریف هر که از یاری برید / پرده‌هایش پرده‌های ما درید
english_translation: The reed is the companion of all who are severed from a friend / Its veils have torn away our veils.
theme: Shared suffering in separation creates profound understanding and empathy

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: من به هر جمعیتی نالان شدم / جفت بدحالان و خوش‌حالان شدم
english_translation: I lamented in every gathering / I paired with those in misery and with those in joy.
theme: Universal compassion that transcends the distinction between joy and sorrow

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: عشق بر دریای غم کشتی بود / عاشقی را عشق کافی بود
english_translation: Love is a ship upon the sea of sorrow / For the lover, love alone is sufficient.
theme: Love as the only vessel that can navigate the seas of sorrow

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: پس چه باید کرد ای اقوام شرق؟ / گم شدن در موج این دریای فرق
english_translation: So what must be done, O Eastern peoples? / To lose oneself in the waves of this sea of distinction.
theme: The dissolution of the ego-self as the ultimate spiritual act

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: مرده بودم زنده شدم، گریه بودم خنده شدم / دولت عشق آمد و من دولت پاینده شدم
english_translation: I was dead, I came alive; I was weeping, I became laughing / The fortune of love came, and I became an enduring fortune.
theme: Love as the divine force that resurrects the dead soul into vibrant life

author: Hafez (Khwaja Shams-ud-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi)
persian: آن که پیش از این دل من سوخت از عشق / الله الله چه حریف بی‌محابا
english_translation: The one who burned my heart with love before this / God, God, what a bold and fearless companion.
theme: The reckless courage of true love that burns without restraint

author: Hafez (Khwaja Shams-ud-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi)
persian: رسید مژده که ایام غم نخواهد ماند / چنین نماند و چنین هم نخواهد ماند
english_translation: Good news arrived: the days of sorrow will not remain / It did not remain so and it will not remain so.
theme: All sorrow is temporary — nothing remains forever, not even suffering

author: Hafez (Khwaja Shams-ud-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi)
persian: ای دل غمین مباش که این گنبد مینا / بر هیچ کس نماند و بر هیچ کس نخواهد ماند
english_translation: O grieving heart, be not sorrowful, for this azure dome / Did not remain for anyone, and will not remain for anyone.
theme: The impermanence of the cosmos as consolation for personal grief

author: Hafez (Khwaja Shams-ud-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi)
persian: واعظان کاین جلوه در محراب و منبر می‌کنند / چون به خلوت می‌روند آن کار دیگر می‌کنند
english_translation: The preachers who display piety in the mosque and pulpit / When they go into private, they do something altogether different.
theme: The gap between public piety and private conduct as the essence of hypocrisy

author: Hafez (Khwaja Shams-ud-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi)
persian: گر مسلمانی از این است که حافظ دارد / آه اگر از پس امروز بود فردایی
english_translation: If Islam is what Hafez has / Alas, if there is a tomorrow after today.
theme: Honest self-examination of one's spiritual shortcomings

author: Hafez (Khwaja Shams-ud-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi)
persian: شکر خدا که هر چه طلب کردم، یافتم / کام جوان بر آمد و مقصد میسر شد
english_translation: Thanks be to God that everything I sought, I found / The wish of youth was fulfilled and the goal was achieved.
theme: Gratitude to the divine for the fulfillment of sincere seeking

author: Hafez (Khwaja Shams-ud-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi)
persian: هر که آمد عالمی آراست رفت / ما که داریم این جهان را؟
english_translation: Everyone who came adorned a world and departed / What do we own of this world?
theme: The transience of all human achievement in the face of mortality

author: Hafez (Khwaja Shams-ud-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi)
persian: الا ای آهوی وحشی کجایی؟ / مرا با تو است چندین آشنایی
english_translation: O wild deer, where are you? / I have so much familiarity with you.
theme: The soul's kinship with wild, untameable freedom

author: Saadi Shirazi (Muslih ud-Din Mushrif ibn Abdullah Shirazi)
persian: نشاید که گویی ندارم توان / چو گفتن توانی که ندارم توان
english_translation: You should not say 'I have no capacity' / For you have the capacity to say 'I have no capacity.'
theme: The hidden capacity that disproves all claims of inability

author: Saadi Shirazi (Muslih ud-Din Mushrif ibn Abdullah Shirazi)
persian: تو آن مرغی که می‌دانی که گفتی / چرا در بند می‌مانی ز دستی
english_translation: You are that bird that knows how to speak / Why then do you remain in the hand's cage?
theme: The tragedy of remaining imprisoned when you possess the power to be free

author: Saadi Shirazi (Muslih ud-Din Mushrif ibn Abdullah Shirazi)
persian: چه خوش بود که بعد از این نیک کنم / بدی‌هایم را با نیکی تلافی کنم
english_translation: How good it would be if from now on I do good / And compensate for my wrongs with goodness.
theme: The power of choosing goodness as a redemption for past wrongs

author: Saadi Shirazi (Muslih ud-Din Mushrif ibn Abdullah Shirazi)
persian: بسیار سفر باید تا پخته شود خامی / صوفی نشود صافی تا در سفر نیاید
english_translation: Much travel is needed for the raw to become mature / The Sufi does not become refined until he undertakes a journey.
theme: Life experience and travel as the essential forge of wisdom and maturity

author: Saadi Shirazi (Muslih ud-Din Mushrif ibn Abdullah Shirazi)
persian: کریم الطبع دشوار آزار گیرد / ولی چون برآشفت، دشوار آرام گیرد
english_translation: A generous spirit is slow to be offended / But once stirred, it is slow to calm down.
theme: The nature of the truly patient — slow to anger but deeply felt when crossed

author: Saadi Shirazi (Muslih ud-Din Mushrif ibn Abdullah Shirazi)
persian: یکی نغز گفت از سر راستی / که بیماری راحت است از کاهلی
english_translation: Someone wisely said with sincerity / That illness of the body comes from laziness of the soul.
theme: Spiritual and physical laziness as root causes of decline and illness

author: Omar Khayyam (Ghiyath ad-Din Abu'l-Fath Umar ibn Ibrahim al-Khayyam Nishapuri)
persian: گویند کسان بهشت با حور خوش است / من می‌گویم که آب انگور خوش است
english_translation: People say paradise with houris is delightful / I say that the juice of the grape is delightful.
theme: Preferring present earthly pleasures over speculative future rewards

author: Omar Khayyam (Ghiyath ad-Din Abu'l-Fath Umar ibn Ibrahim al-Khayyam Nishapuri)
persian: یک قطره آب بود با دریا شد / یک ذره خاک بود با صحرا شد
english_translation: A drop of water was, and became the sea / A grain of dust was, and became the desert.
theme: The individual merging with the universal — the journey from smallness to vastness

author: Omar Khayyam (Ghiyath ad-Din Abu'l-Fath Umar ibn Ibrahim al-Khayyam Nishapuri)
persian: چون عمر به سر رسد چه بغداد و چه بلخ / پیمانه چو پر شد چه شیرین و چه تلخ
english_translation: When life comes to its end, what matter Baghdad or Balkh / When the cup is full, what matter sweet or bitter.
theme: Death as the great equalizer that renders all earthly distinctions meaningless

author: Omar Khayyam (Ghiyath ad-Din Abu'l-Fath Umar ibn Ibrahim al-Khayyam Nishapuri)
persian: می نوش که بعد از من و تو ماه بسی / از سلخ به غره شود از غره به سلخ
english_translation: Drink wine, for after you and I, the moon will many times / Pass from full to new and from new to full.
theme: The endless continuation of cosmic cycles after our passing, urging present joy

author: Omar Khayyam (Ghiyath ad-Din Abu'l-Fath Umar ibn Ibrahim al-Khayyam Nishapuri)
persian: نیکی و بدی که در نهاد بشر است / شادی و غمی که در قضا و قدر است
english_translation: The good and evil that lie in human nature / The joy and sorrow in fate and destiny.
theme: The inseparable duality of good and evil, joy and sorrow, in human fate

author: Ferdowsi (Abu'l-Qasim Ferdowsi Tusi)
persian: مکن بد که بد بینی اندر جهان / که تخم بدی را بروید زمان
english_translation: Do no evil, lest you see evil in the world / For time will cause the seed of evil to sprout.
theme: Evil actions as seeds that time inevitably causes to grow and bear bitter fruit

author: Ferdowsi (Abu'l-Qasim Ferdowsi Tusi)
persian: دانش و دین یار یکدیگر بوند / هر دو با هم تاج افسر بوند
english_translation: Knowledge and faith are companions of one another / Together they form the crown of excellence.
theme: Knowledge and faith as complementary companions that together create excellence

author: Ferdowsi (Abu'l-Qasim Ferdowsi Tusi)
persian: زبان را نگه دار در زیر دندان / که چون تیر رفته نیاید به کمان
english_translation: Guard your tongue behind your teeth / For like an arrow that has been fired, it cannot return to the bow.
theme: Words, like arrows, once released cannot be taken back

author: Ferdowsi (Abu'l-Qasim Ferdowsi Tusi)
persian: سر مرد گردد سخن چون دراز / از اندک سخن گفتن آید نیاز
english_translation: A man's head is turned by speech when it is prolonged / From speaking little comes what is needed.
theme: Brevity in speech as a mark of wisdom and practical necessity

author: Ferdowsi (Abu'l-Qasim Ferdowsi Tusi)
persian: چنین گفت موبد که مرد دروغ‌زن / نگردد کبیر اندر انجمن
english_translation: Thus spoke the wise man: the liar / Will never become great in the assembly.
theme: Dishonesty as an insurmountable obstacle to true greatness and respect

author: Nizami Ganjavi (Ilyas ibn Yusuf ibn Zaki Muayyad)
persian: از محبت خارها گل می‌شود / از محبت سرکه‌ها مل می‌شود
english_translation: Through love, thorns become roses / Through love, vinegar becomes wine.
theme: Love as a divine alchemy that transforms bitterness and pain into beauty

author: Nizami Ganjavi (Ilyas ibn Yusuf ibn Zaki Muayyad)
persian: چو گنج عشق در دل داشتی / همه عالم از آن آباد داشتی
english_translation: When you carry the treasure of love in your heart / You hold the entire world in a state of flourishing.
theme: Love as an inner treasure that enriches one's entire relationship with the world

author: Nizami Ganjavi (Ilyas ibn Yusuf ibn Zaki Muayyad)
persian: هر کسی کو دور ماند از اصل خویش / باز می‌جوید روزگار وصل خویش
english_translation: Whoever remains apart from their true origin / Seeks again the era of reunion.
theme: The eternal yearning to return to one's true origin and nature

author: Nizami Ganjavi (Ilyas ibn Yusuf ibn Zaki Muayyad)
persian: مرد با همت بلند است در جهان / که رسد بر اوج آرزوی خویشتن
english_translation: The person of high ambition stands tall in the world / Who reaches the peak of their own desires.
theme: High ambition and the determination to reach the peaks of one's aspirations

author: Attar of Nishapur (Farid ud-Din Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Attar Nishapuri)
persian: چون دل پاک باشد، راه پاک باشد / وقت پاک باشد، نگاه پاک باشد
english_translation: When the heart is pure, the path is pure / When the moment is pure, the vision is pure.
theme: Inner purity of heart as the source of clear perception and a righteous path

author: Attar of Nishapur (Farid ud-Din Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Attar Nishapuri)
persian: در همه ذرات جهان خورشیدی است / آن که بیناست، بیند این را هشیار
english_translation: In every atom of the world, there is a sun / One who is truly awake will see this clearly.
theme: Divine light as present in every particle of existence for those who are awake

author: Attar of Nishapur (Farid ud-Din Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Attar Nishapuri)
persian: مرغ روحم در قفس دارم نگاه / کی برد این مرغ را خورشید راه
english_translation: I keep the bird of my soul in a cage / When will the sun of the path liberate this bird?
theme: The soul's imprisonment in the ego-self and its longing for divine liberation

author: Attar of Nishapur (Farid ud-Din Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Attar Nishapuri)
persian: تو خود حجاب خودی حافظ از میان برخیز
english_translation: You yourself are the veil between yourself and the divine — rise from the midst.
theme: The ego-self as the only true barrier between the human and the divine

author: Attar of Nishapur (Farid ud-Din Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Attar Nishapuri)
persian: عشق را هفتاد و دو ملت بهانه است / عاشقی مذهب جداگانه است
english_translation: Love has seventy-two nations as its pretexts / Lovingness itself is a separate religion.
theme: Love as a universal religion that transcends all sectarian divisions

author: Ibn Sina (Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah ibn Sina / Avicenna)
persian: طبیب که خود بیمار است، درمان کدام است؟
english_translation: What cure does a physician have who is himself sick?
theme: The necessity of healing oneself before presuming to heal others

author: Ibn Sina (Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah ibn Sina / Avicenna)
persian: انسان از دو چیز ساخته شده: تن و روح / تن نیازمند خوراک است و روح نیازمند حکمت
english_translation: A human is made of two things: body and soul / The body needs food, and the soul needs wisdom.
theme: The dual nourishment required by human beings — food for the body, wisdom for the soul

author: Ibn Sina (Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah ibn Sina / Avicenna)
persian: عقل اول بپرس، سپس بگو / تا ندانی، لب ز گفتار فرو
english_translation: First ask your reason, then speak / Until you know, keep your lips from speaking.
theme: Rational inquiry as the prerequisite for all meaningful speech

author: Ibn Sina (Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah ibn Sina / Avicenna)
persian: فضیلت در علم است و عمل / نه در نژاد و اصل و نسب
english_translation: Virtue lies in knowledge and action / Not in race, origin, or lineage.
theme: True virtue is earned through knowledge and action, not inherited through lineage

author: Al-Biruni (Abu Rayhan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Biruni)
persian: دانستن سود دارد، نه دانستن زیان
english_translation: Knowing is beneficial; not knowing is harmful.
theme: Knowledge as always beneficial and ignorance as always harmful

author: Al-Biruni (Abu Rayhan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Biruni)
persian: هر پدیده‌ای علتی دارد / و هر علتی را می‌توان یافت
english_translation: Every phenomenon has a cause / And every cause can be found.
theme: The rational and discoverable nature of all causality in the universe

author: Al-Biruni (Abu Rayhan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Biruni)
persian: آنچه نمی‌دانی را بگوی نمی‌دانم / که این خود نوعی دانش است
english_translation: Say 'I do not know' to what you do not know / For this itself is a form of knowledge.
theme: Admitting ignorance honestly as itself a form of genuine wisdom

author: Naser Khosrow (Abu Mu'in Hamid ad-Din Nasir ibn Khusraw al-Qubadiyani Marvazi)
persian: کسی که با دانش نشست، دانا شد / کسی که با نادان نشست، نادان شد
english_translation: He who sat with the learned became learned / He who sat with the ignorant became ignorant.
theme: The transformative power of one's intellectual and social environment

author: Naser Khosrow (Abu Mu'in Hamid ad-Din Nasir ibn Khusraw al-Qubadiyani Marvazi)
persian: هر که حق گوید، حق‌اش پیدا شود / هر که باطل گوید، باطل‌اش نمایان شود
english_translation: Whoever speaks truth, their truth will become manifest / Whoever speaks falsehood, their falsehood will become apparent.
theme: The inevitable manifestation of both truth and falsehood over time

author: Sanai Ghaznavi (Abu al-Majd Majdud ibn Adam Sana'i Ghaznavi)
persian: تا نگردی آشنا زین پرده، راز نشنوی / دل پاک کن که این آیینه را گرد نشنوی
english_translation: Until you become familiar with this veil, you will hear no secret / Purify the heart, for you will not hear the dust on this mirror.
theme: Spiritual purity as the prerequisite for receiving divine secrets

author: Sanai Ghaznavi (Abu al-Majd Majdud ibn Adam Sana'i Ghaznavi)
persian: خوش بود گر محک تجربه آید به میان / تا سیه‌روی شود هر که در او غش باشد
english_translation: It would be good if the touchstone of experience came forth / So that whoever has impurity within them would be exposed.
theme: Experience as the ultimate touchstone that reveals true character and hidden flaws

author: Jami (Nur ad-Din Abd ar-Rahman ibn Ahmad Jami)
persian: دوست آن است که گیرد دست دوست / در پریشان‌حالی و درماندگی
english_translation: A friend is one who takes the hand of a friend / In times of distress and helplessness.
theme: True friendship defined by presence and support in times of greatest need

author: Jami (Nur ad-Din Abd ar-Rahman ibn Ahmad Jami)
persian: کمال انسان نه در ثروت است نه در قدرت / بلکه در معرفت و محبت است
english_translation: Human perfection lies not in wealth or power / But in knowledge and love.
theme: True human perfection measured by love and knowledge rather than power or wealth

author: Jami (Nur ad-Din Abd ar-Rahman ibn Ahmad Jami)
persian: هر که را دل پاک بود، زندگی‌اش پاک بود / هر که را دل کج بود، راهش کج بود
english_translation: Whoever has a pure heart has a pure life / Whoever has a crooked heart has a crooked path.
theme: The heart as the source that determines the quality and direction of one's life

author: Rudaki (Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad Rudaki Samarkandi)
persian: هر که نکوتر زیست، او را بیشتر جای است در یاد
english_translation: Whoever lived more beautifully occupies more space in memory.
theme: A beautiful life as the most enduring claim on the memory of posterity

author: Rudaki (Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad Rudaki Samarkandi)
persian: علم داری، عمل کن، که علم بی‌عمل / مانند درختی است که میوه ندارد
english_translation: If you have knowledge, act upon it, for knowledge without action / Is like a tree that bears no fruit.
theme: Knowledge that is not put into action is sterile and without value

author: Hakim Owhadi Maraghei
persian: قدر وقت ار نشناسد دل و کاری نکند / این همه راه که آمد، همه را باز رود
english_translation: If the heart does not know the value of time and does nothing / All the road it has traveled, it will travel back again.
theme: Failure to act decisively in time leads only to wasted effort and regression

author: Amir Khusrow Dehlavi (Abu'l Hasan Yamīn ud-Dīn Khusraw)
persian: در هجر مهرویان، دل بسوزد آتشین / چون شمع می‌گدازد اندر آتش یقین
english_translation: In the absence of a sun-faced beloved, the heart burns fiercely / Like a candle melting in the fire of certainty.
theme: The burning intensity of the heart that endures the absence of the beloved

author: Amir Khusrow Dehlavi (Abu'l Hasan Yamīn ud-Dīn Khusraw)
persian: زبان شیرین، دل آدم را نرم کند / زبان تلخ، دل آدم را سخت کند
english_translation: Sweet speech softens a person's heart / Bitter speech hardens a person's heart.
theme: The power of gentle speech to open hearts and of harsh speech to close them

author: Parvin E'tesami
persian: گهر پیدا کن اندر ژرف دریا / اگر آسایش دیدار خواهی
english_translation: Find the pearl in the depths of the sea / If you desire the peace of true vision.
theme: True treasures require the courage to dive into the deepest depths

author: Parvin E'tesami
persian: ستم‌دیده را تان و توان بیشتر است / که زیر بار ستم، جان می‌شود محکم‌تر
english_translation: The oppressed have greater strength and capacity / For under the burden of oppression, the soul becomes stronger.
theme: Suffering and oppression as the forge that tempers and strengthens the human soul

author: Forough Farrokhzad
persian: در شب تاریک، روشنایی را باید یافت / که آفتاب هر روز از نو می‌درخشد
english_translation: In the dark night, one must find the light / For the sun shines anew each day.
theme: Hope as the light that must actively be sought in the darkest of times

author: Ahmad Shamlu
persian: وقتی که می‌خندی، دنیا می‌خندد با تو / وقتی که گریه می‌کنی، تنها گریه می‌کنی
english_translation: When you laugh, the world laughs with you / When you cry, you cry alone.
theme: The social truth that joy is shared while sorrow is often borne alone

author: Ahmad Shamlu
persian: انسان را شناختن، خود را شناختن است
english_translation: To know a human being is to know oneself.
theme: The deep connection between understanding others and understanding oneself

author: Sohrab Sepehri
persian: چشم‌ها را باید شست / جور دیگر باید دید
english_translation: One must wash one's eyes / One must see differently.
theme: The necessity of cleansing one's perception to see the world truly and freshly

author: Sohrab Sepehri
persian: زندگی یعنی که تنها باشی / زندگی یعنی که آزاد باشی
english_translation: Life means being alone / Life means being free.
theme: Solitude and freedom as the twin pillars of authentic human existence

author: Sohrab Sepehri
persian: به باغ آمدم، درختان را دیدم / بوی گل دادند، آب را شنیدم
english_translation: I came to the garden, I saw the trees / They gave off the fragrance of flowers, I heard the water.
theme: Full sensory presence in nature as a form of awakened consciousness

author: Nizam al-Mulk (Abu Ali Hasan ibn Ali Tusi, Seljuk Vizier)
persian: آن پادشاه که به مردم ظلم کند / پادشاهی‌اش دیری نپاید
english_translation: A king who oppresses his people / His kingship will not last long.
theme: Oppression as the seed of a ruler's own inevitable downfall

author: Nizam al-Mulk (Abu Ali Hasan ibn Ali Tusi, Seljuk Vizier)
persian: وزیر خردمند، سلطان را بزرگ کند / وزیر نادان، سلطان را کوچک کند
english_translation: A wise minister makes the sultan great / A foolish minister makes the sultan small.
theme: The critical importance of wise counsel in determining a leader's greatness or failure

author: Al-Ghazali (Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Ghazali)
persian: اگر به دنبال خوشبختی می‌گردی، به درون خود نگاه کن / چرا که خوشبختی در بیرون از تو نیست
english_translation: If you are looking for happiness, look within yourself / For happiness does not lie outside of you.
theme: Happiness as an inner state that can only be found through self-inquiry

author: Al-Ghazali (Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Ghazali)
persian: دنیا مزرعه آخرت است
english_translation: This world is the field of the hereafter.
theme: The present life as a field in which one plants the seeds of eternal consequence

author: Al-Ghazali (Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Ghazali)
persian: ستودن خود نشانه نادانی است / شکستن دیگران نشانه ضعف است
english_translation: Praising yourself is a sign of ignorance / Belittling others is a sign of weakness.
theme: Self-aggrandizement and the disparagement of others as signs of ignorance and weakness

author: Abu Said Abil Kheir (Abu Said ibn Abi'l-Khayr)
persian: هر که شد محرم دل، در حرم یار نشست / که حرم درگه اسرار دل‌افروز من است
english_translation: Whoever becomes privy to the heart's secrets, sits in the beloved's sanctuary / For the sanctuary is the threshold of the secrets that kindle my heart.
theme: The innermost heart as the sacred sanctuary where the divine is truly encountered

author: Abu Said Abil Kheir (Abu Said ibn Abi'l-Khayr)
persian: گر مرد رهی، میان خون باید رفت / از پای در آمده سرنگون باید رفت
english_translation: If you are a traveler of the path, you must go through blood / You must go tumbling headlong where feet fail.
theme: The spiritual path demands total sacrifice, even to the point of complete surrender

author: Baba Tahir Hamadani
persian: دلم غرق درد است از دوری یار / که دوری چو آتش بسوزد دلم زار
english_translation: My heart is drowning in pain from the distance of my beloved / For distance, like fire, burns my wretched heart.
theme: The consuming fire of longing caused by distance from one's beloved

author: Baba Tahir Hamadani
persian: اگر صد سال خوانی علم و حکمت / ولی مهرت نباشد، کور و کر مان
english_translation: If you study knowledge and wisdom for a hundred years / But have no love, you remain blind and deaf.
theme: Love as the sense that gives sight and hearing to all accumulated knowledge

author: Nasir al-Din Tusi (Khwaja Nasir al-Din Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi)
persian: انسان کامل کسی است که عقل او بر هوای نفس غلبه کند
english_translation: A perfect human being is one whose reason triumphs over the desires of the ego.
theme: Human perfection defined by the victory of reason over ego-driven desire

author: Nasir al-Din Tusi (Khwaja Nasir al-Din Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi)
persian: سعادت در سه چیز است: علم، عمل، و اخلاق
english_translation: Happiness lies in three things: knowledge, action, and moral character.
theme: The threefold formula for genuine happiness — knowledge, action, and virtue

author: Persian Proverb
persian: درخت هر قدر بلندتر باشد، ریشه‌اش عمیق‌تر است
english_translation: The taller the tree, the deeper its roots.
theme: True height and achievement are supported by correspondingly deep foundations

author: Persian Proverb
persian: ماهی از سر گنده گردد نی ز دم
english_translation: A fish rots from the head, not from the tail.
theme: Leadership and those at the top bear primary responsibility for institutional decay

author: Persian Proverb
persian: آب از سرچشمه صاف است
english_translation: Water is pure at its source.
theme: Things are most pure and true at their origin before being corrupted by distance

author: Persian Proverb
persian: اگر کوه به کوه نمی‌رسد، آدم به آدم می‌رسد
english_translation: If mountain does not meet mountain, person meets person.
theme: Human beings inevitably find one another even when circumstances seem impossible

author: Persian Proverb
persian: عروس نشان می‌دهند، عیب پنهان می‌کنند
english_translation: The bride is shown; her faults are hidden.
theme: The universal tendency to present the best face while concealing true shortcomings

author: Persian Proverb
persian: با یک گل بهار نمی‌شود
english_translation: With a single flower, spring does not arrive.
theme: No single effort alone is sufficient — great things require collective contribution

author: Persian Proverb
persian: صبر تلخ است ولی ثمره‌اش شیرین
english_translation: Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet.
theme: The bitterness of patience is always redeemed by the sweetness of its eventual reward

author: Persian Proverb
persian: سنگ بزرگ نشان نزدن است
english_translation: A large stone is a sign of not being thrown.
theme: Grandiose plans that are never executed are worse than modest ones fulfilled

author: Persian Proverb
persian: گاو پیشانی سفید را همه می‌شناسند
english_translation: Everyone knows the cow with the white forehead.
theme: Those with distinctive character or reputation cannot hide or remain unknown

author: Persian Proverb
persian: آتش که گرفت، خشک و تر می‌سوزد
english_translation: When fire catches, it burns both the dry and the wet.
theme: Uncontrolled destructive forces make no distinction between the innocent and guilty

author: Persian Proverb
persian: کار نیکو کردن از پر کردن است
english_translation: Doing good work comes from filling oneself first.
theme: One must first fill oneself with knowledge and virtue before doing truly good work

author: Persian Proverb
persian: حرف مرد یکی است
english_translation: A man's word is one (i.e., a person of honor keeps their word).
theme: Integrity of character is measured by the consistency between one's words and deeds

author: Persian Proverb
persian: دوری و دوستی
english_translation: Distance and friendship (i.e., absence makes the heart grow fonder).
theme: Occasional separation can strengthen the bonds of friendship and love

author: Persian Proverb
persian: شتر در خواب بیند پنبه‌دانه / گهی لپ لپ خورد گه دانه دانه
english_translation: The camel dreams of cotton fields / Sometimes it eats in gulps, sometimes grain by grain.
theme: The vast gap between what we dream of and the modest reality we actually inhabit

author: Persian Proverb
persian: هر که بامش بیش، برفش بیشتر
english_translation: Whoever has the bigger roof, has more snow on it.
theme: Greater privilege, status, or wealth comes with proportionally greater burden and responsibility

author: Persian Proverb
persian: نه سیخ بسوزد، نه کباب
english_translation: Neither the skewer burns nor the kebab (i.e., doing things with wisdom to avoid all losses).
theme: True wisdom finds solutions where no one loses and all interests are preserved

author: Persian Proverb
persian: آدم عاقل عبرت می‌گیرد، آدم احمق پشیمان می‌شود
english_translation: A wise person learns a lesson; a foolish person only regrets.
theme: Wisdom converts experience into lessons while foolishness converts it into mere regret

author: Persian Proverb
persian: در بسته را که باز کند؟ مگر کلید
english_translation: Who can open a locked door? Only a key.
theme: Every problem has a specific solution; the task is finding the right key

author: Persian Proverb
persian: هر نی که خورد زهر، تریاکش هم هست
english_translation: For every poison that a reed drinks, its antidote also exists.
theme: For every harm or poison in the world, a corresponding remedy also exists

author: Persian Proverb
persian: شیر را در قفس پرورش ندهند
english_translation: A lion is not raised in a cage.
theme: True greatness and wild potential cannot flourish within confining environments

author: Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi
persian: من آنم که می‌دانم که نمی‌دانم
english_translation: I am the one who knows that he does not know.
theme: The Socratic acknowledgment that true knowledge begins with knowing one's own ignorance

author: Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi
persian: زبان شمشیر است، از آن مراقب باش / که زخمش از زخم تیغ دیرتر بهبود یابد
english_translation: The tongue is a sword, guard it carefully / For its wound heals more slowly than the wound of a blade.
theme: Words wound more deeply and heal more slowly than any physical blade

author: Qabus ibn Wushmagir (Amir Shams al-Ma'ali Qabus ibn Wushmagir)
persian: هر که را صبر است، کامروا شود / ثمره صبر همیشه شیرین بود
english_translation: Whoever has patience will have their wishes fulfilled / The fruit of patience is always sweet.
theme: Patience as the guaranteed path to the fulfillment of one's deepest wishes

author: Qabus ibn Wushmagir (Amir Shams al-Ma'ali Qabus ibn Wushmagir)
persian: آنچه در قلبت داری، روز به روز بر زبانت می‌آید
english_translation: What you carry in your heart comes to your tongue day by day.
theme: The inner content of the heart inevitably reveals itself through speech over time

author: Rashid al-Din Fadlallah
persian: دانش بدون حکمت، خطرناک است
english_translation: Knowledge without wisdom is dangerous.
theme: Raw knowledge unguided by moral wisdom becomes a dangerous instrument

author: Rashid al-Din Fadlallah
persian: آنچه برای خود نمی‌پسندی برای دیگران هم مپسند
english_translation: What you do not wish for yourself, do not wish for others.
theme: The Golden Rule: empathy and reciprocity as the foundation of all ethics

author: Manuchehri Damghani
persian: بهار آمد، گل‌ها شکفتند / دل را به شادی وا کن، که دنیا تازه شد
english_translation: Spring has come, the flowers have bloomed / Open your heart to joy, for the world is renewed.
theme: Spring as a divine invitation to open the heart to renewal and joy

author: Auhad ud-Din Kirmani
persian: سالک آن است که ذره ذره از خود بگذرد / تا به دریای بی‌کران برسد
english_translation: The spiritual seeker is one who passes beyond themselves, particle by particle / Until reaching the boundless sea.
theme: The spiritual journey as a gradual dissolution of the self into the infinite divine

author: Auhad ud-Din Kirmani
persian: محبت کن به هر ذره که بینی / که در هر ذره‌ای، خورشیدی نهفته است
english_translation: Love every particle that you see / For within every particle, a sun is hidden.
theme: Divine love revealed in every particle of existence to the awakened eye

author: Hakim Sanai
persian: طالب دیدار حق، چون حق شود / از همه عالم جدا و متفق
english_translation: The seeker of the divine vision, when becoming divine / Becomes both separate from the whole world and united with it.
theme: The paradox of the divine seeker who, in union, becomes both separate and one with all

author: Hakim Sanai
persian: چون نمی‌دانی کجا خواهی رسید / خود برو، ره خود به خود می‌دانی دید
english_translation: Since you do not know where you will arrive / Just go — the path reveals itself to you as you travel.
theme: The courage to begin walking without knowing the destination, trusting the path to reveal itself

author: Iraj Mirza
persian: از مادر خود شرم نیست کردن / با مهر مادر، دنیا گلستان شود
english_translation: It is no shame to be devoted to one's mother / Through a mother's love, the world becomes a garden of roses.
theme: Maternal love as the original and most transformative love that makes the world bloom

author: Khaqani Shirwani (Afzal ad-Din Ibrahim ibn Ali Najjar Khaqani Shirwani)
persian: تاج شاهان از زر است و سیم و گوهر / تاج فرزانه از علم است و هنر
english_translation: The crown of kings is made of gold, silver, and gems / The crown of the wise is made of knowledge and art.
theme: The crown of wisdom, made of knowledge and art, exceeds any crown of worldly power

author: Anvari (Awhad ud-Din Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ardashir Anvari Abivardi)
persian: ای که یک عمر تمنای سخن داری و بس / هنر آن نیست که گویی، هنر آن است که دانی
english_translation: O you who spend a lifetime only craving to speak / The art is not in speaking, the art is in knowing.
theme: True artistry lies in depth of knowledge rather than in the volume of speech

author: Anvari (Awhad ud-Din Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ardashir Anvari Abivardi)
persian: کمال مرد در سخن است و در خرد / نه در مال و جاه و زر و سیم و خرد
english_translation: A man's perfection lies in his speech and his reason / Not in wealth, status, gold, silver, and possessions.
theme: Eloquence and rational wisdom as the true measure of a person's worth and perfection

author: Nezami Aruzi Samarqandi
persian: آن کس که در راه دانش گام زد / از تاریکی جهالت رهایی یافت
english_translation: The one who walked the path of knowledge / Found liberation from the darkness of ignorance.
theme: The pursuit of knowledge as the path from the darkness of ignorance into liberating light

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: دی شیخ با چراغ همی‌گشت گرد شهر / کز دیو و دد ملولم و انسانم آرزوست
english_translation: Yesterday the Sheikh wandered around the city with a lantern / Saying: I am weary of demons and beasts — I yearn for a human being.
theme: The rarity of true human beings who possess genuine virtue, compassion, and wisdom

author: Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi)
persian: مولوی هرگز نخواند جز دل / کو نخوانده است همیشه کتاب دل
english_translation: Rumi never read anything but the heart / For he who has not read the book of the heart, has not truly read.
theme: The heart as the supreme and most essential text, surpassing all written books

author: Hafez (Khwaja Shams-ud-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi)
persian: همه کس طالب یارند، چه هشیار و چه مست / همه جا خانه عشق است، چه مسجد چه کنشت
english_translation: Everyone seeks the beloved, whether sober or drunk / Everywhere is the house of love, whether mosque or synagogue.
theme: Love as the universal human seeking that transcends all religious boundaries
